items.issue: The explain command sorts by {createdAt:-1} only, but the same commit changed OperatorService.list to sort by createdAt DESC .and(id DESC), so the test explains a query shape production never issues. Verified against mongo:7.0 with 200 seeded docs: the test's shape wins LIMIT/FETCH/IXSCAN(org_status_created), while the real shape {createdAt:-1,_id:-1} wins a blocking SORT stage (type simple, memLimit 100MB) above the IXSCAN — every ACTIVE row for the org is fetched and sorted in memory before the limit applies. The assertions still pass under both shapes, so the test gives false assurance for the Javadoc claim that org_status_created serves the newest-first production read.
items.fix: Build the explain sort from the production shape — .append("sort", new Document("createdAt", -1).append("_id", -1)) — and assert the winning plan has no SORT stage as well as no COLLSCAN; that will go red until the index def in Address.java is extended to {'organisationId':1,'status':1,'createdAt':-1,'_id':-1} (or the id tie-breaker is dropped).
